figures.name: Phi Fa

ability.name: Lightning Spirit
ability.description: Deal 7 damage to all enemy cards simultaneously with a lightning strike.

figures.description: The sky spirit of Lao belief who governs thunder and lightning, propitiated during storms and before the rainy season.

figures.name: Khun Borom

ability.name: Heavenly Descent
ability.description: Descend from the sky bringing all foundational resources; all allied cards gain 2 to all stats.

figures.description: The heavenly ancestor of the Lao people who descended from the sky with his gourd of rice, founder of the royal lineage and agriculture.

figures.name: Nang Thorani (Lao)

ability.name: Earth Witness
ability.description: Call on the earth to witness; all deception and illusion effects on the field are nullified.

figures.description: The earth goddess in Lao Buddhism, identical to the Thai Mae Thorani, whose hair-wringing drove away Mara's armies during the Buddha's enlightenment.

figures.name: Phra Lak

ability.name: Devoted Brother
ability.description: Shield the strongest allied card from all attacks for 1 turn; take all damage instead.

figures.description: The Lao version of Lakshmana, devoted brother of Phra Ram, whose loyalty and martial skill are celebrated in the Lao Ramayana Pha Lak Pha Lam.

figures.name: Phra Ram (Lao)

ability.name: Sacred Bow
ability.description: Fire an arrow that never misses; deal 9 damage to the enemy with the highest defense.

figures.description: The Lao version of Rama, the great hero of the Pha Lak Pha Lam epic, whose journey and battles take on uniquely Lao characteristics.

figures.name: Nang Sida (Lao)

ability.name: Earth Daughter Purity
ability.description: Purify the entire field; all dark effects and curses are removed.

figures.description: The Lao Sita, whose purity and devotion are central to the Lao Ramayana, proven by her return to the earth at the story's end.

figures.name: Thaen

ability.name: World Creation
ability.description: Create any terrain or environment card; it persists for the entire game.

figures.description: The creator god of Lao cosmology, ruler of the sky realm, who sent rice down to humans and established the cosmic order.

figures.name: Mangkhalasena

ability.name: War Elephant
ability.description: Charge all enemies with an elephant; deal 7 damage to the front row of enemies.

figures.description: A great Lao warrior hero celebrated in temple murals, riding into battle on a war elephant in defense of the Lao kingdom.

figures.name: Naga (Lao)

ability.name: Mekong Guardian
ability.description: Control the Mekong; increase all water resources by 3 and prevent enemy water use.

figures.description: The great naga of the Mekong River, central to Lao identity, whose fire bubbles at the naga fireballs festival signal the rainy season's end.

figures.name: Ketsana

ability.name: Dragon Quest
ability.description: Embark on a quest; reveal three cards from the deck and take the one you need most.

figures.description: A Lao hero of epic tales who battles dragons and supernatural forces, representing the bravery of the common hero in Lao folklore.

figures.name: Phi Pop (Lao)

ability.name: Village Curse
ability.description: Spread illness; all enemy cards in one row lose 2 HP per turn for 2 turns.

figures.description: The possessing spirit of Lao belief that causes illness, feared throughout villages, similar to the Thai Phi Phop.

figures.name: Nang Ae Nang Kham

ability.name: Golden Fortune
ability.description: Grant 3 fortune tokens to allied cards; each token can be spent for +2 to any stat.

figures.description: The golden spirit girl who brings fortune and beauty, propitiated in Lao homes for good luck and prosperity.

figures.name: Pou Gnoe Gna Gnoe

ability.name: Ancestral Visit
ability.description: Ancestral spirits visit; all allied cards are healed for 4 HP at the New Year moment.

figures.description: The ancestral spirits who visit during the Lao New Year, bringing blessings from the realm of the ancestors to the living.

figures.name: Indra (Lao)

ability.name: Heavenly Army
ability.description: Summon a celestial army; deal 5 damage to all enemies and grant all allies +2 defense.

figures.description: Indra as revered in Lao Buddhism, lord of the Tavatimsa heaven and protector of righteous kings, whose sacred mount is the elephant.

figures.name: Yama (Lao)

ability.name: Ledger of Deeds
ability.description: Read one card's history; deal damage equal to karmic debt accumulated this game.

figures.description: The Lao lord of the dead who maintains the book of deeds, judging souls after death and determining their next incarnation.

figures.name: Kalakeya

ability.name: War Demons
ability.description: Release a horde of war demons; all enemy cards are attacked simultaneously for 4 damage each.

figures.description: The demon warriors who appear as obstacles in Lao epic tales, testing the heroes with battle and supernatural challenges.

figures.name: Boon (Merit)

ability.name: Merit Making
ability.description: Gain merit tokens equal to good deeds this turn; spend them for any beneficial effect.

figures.description: The spiritual force of accumulated merit in Lao Buddhism, which protects and elevates those who have performed virtuous deeds.

figures.name: Sin (Demerit)

ability.name: Karmic Debt
ability.description: Place karmic debt on one enemy; they lose 1 stat point for each dark action taken.

figures.description: The accumulated negative karma in Lao Buddhist belief, the counterforce to merit, which leads souls to unfavorable rebirths.

figures.name: Sangkha Nakhon

ability.name: Merchant Voyage
ability.description: Travel to a distant realm; draw 3 cards and gain resources from the journey.

figures.description: A merchant hero of Lao folk tales who undertakes sea voyages and encounters supernatural beings, returning with wisdom and wealth.

figures.name: Pha Lak

ability.name: Elder's Shield
ability.description: Protect all younger allied cards; they cannot be targeted while Pha Lak stands.

figures.description: Variant spelling of Phra Lak, the devoted brother who fights alongside Phra Ram through all dangers in the Lao Ramayana tradition.
